message.content: {"items":[{"term":"6-7","definition":"A deliberately meaningless number shouted as a comedic interruption, often when someone mentions a number near six or seven.","originContext":"The source connects its spread to a song and artist, and to a basketball player whose height became part of the joke.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“6-7” is a deliberately meaningless number that gets shouted whenever someone says a number close to six or seven"}]},{"term":"41","definition":"A related number used more as a contradiction or alternate answer than as a standalone joke.","originContext":"The source presents it as a cousin term to “6-7.”","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“41,” which functions more like a contradiction or an alternate answer than its own separate joke."}]},{"term":"delulu","definition":"Short for “delusional”; describes an overly optimistic or unrealistic belief, often about a crush, job, or fantasy outcome.","originContext":"The source traces its use to K-pop stan culture on Twitter, followed by broader everyday use.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Delulu” is short for delusional, and it almost always describes someone’s own overly optimistic or unrealistic belief"}]},{"term":"crashing out","definition":"Having a visible emotional or behavioral meltdown, often triggered by stress, jealousy, or a breakup.","originContext":"The source describes it as a shift from private frustration into a public escalation.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"To “crash out,” or to have a “crash out,” means having a visible emotional or behavioral meltdown"}]},{"term":"aura farming","definition":"Deliberately acting or moving to look effortlessly cool, often with an implication that the effort is being mocked.","originContext":"The source associates the phrase with sports and gaming clips, where “farming” calls out people trying for a clip.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Aura farming” describes deliberately acting or moving in a way designed to look effortlessly cool"}]},{"term":"canon event","definition":"A moment treated as an unavoidable, defining part of someone’s life story.","originContext":"Borrowed from fandom language about what counts as real in a fictional universe, the phrase moved into everyday life talk.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"A “canon event” is a moment framed as an unavoidable, defining part of someone’s story"}]},{"term":"mewing","definition":"A tongue-posture technique that some people believe sharpens jawline definition.","originContext":"The source says the technique predates its meme status and is named after the orthodontist associated with it.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Mewing” refers to a tongue-posture technique some people believe sharpens jawline definition"}]},{"term":"unc","definition":"A familiar term, usually for a man, or a label for someone acting older, more out of touch, or more cautious than their age suggests.","originContext":"The source traces it to Black American English, where it could be familiar and affectionate before broader internet use.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Unc” describes someone, usually a man, acting older, more out of touch, or more cautious than his actual age suggests"}]},{"term":"brat","definition":"Someone confidently unbothered, somewhat messy, and unapologetically themselves; a newer sense that contrasts with the older meaning of a spoiled child.","originContext":"The source attributes the shift to a pop-culture moment.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Brat” now describes someone confidently unbothered, a little messy, and unapologetically themselves"}]},{"term":"biblically accurate","definition":"Describes something strange, overwhelming, or unsettling, referencing depictions of angels based on scriptural descriptions.","originContext":"The source says an art trend featuring these depictions sparked the meme.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"Calling something “biblically accurate” means it looks strange, overwhelming, or unsettling"}]},{"term":"beige flag","definition":"A personality quirk that is neither a warning sign nor a positive trait, but is mildly odd or forgettable.","originContext":"The source places it in dating vocabulary as a neutral middle ground between red and green flags.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"A “beige flag” is a personality quirk that isn’t a genuine warning sign and isn’t a positive trait either"}]},{"term":"NPC energy","definition":"The impression that someone is following a script or blending into the background, by analogy with a non-player character in a game.","originContext":"The source connects its wider use to a livestream trend mimicking scripted, repetitive behavior.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“NPC energy” describes someone acting like they’re following a script or blending into the background"}]},{"term":"brain rot","definition":"Low-value, low-effort content, or the mentally foggy feeling associated with consuming too much of it.","originContext":"The source describes it as starting as a self-aware joke about scrolling habits before becoming a descriptor for content.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Brain rot” describes low-value, low-effort content, or the mentally foggy feeling that comes from consuming too much of it"}]},{"term":"skibidi","definition":"An absurdist filler word with no fixed meaning.","originContext":"The source roots it in an animated meme series and describes its use as driven by sound and repetition rather than a stable definition.","sources":[{"url":"https://bamfuzzle.com/blog/2026-internet-slang-terms-explained/","quote":"“Skibidi” has no fixed meaning and functions as pure absurdist filler"}]}]}
